item.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
item.description: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future $e^+e^-$ colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes $e^+ e^- \to t\bar{t},\ e^+e^-\to μ^+μ^-$ and Bhabha scattering $e^+e^-\to e^+e^-$, representing the mass threshold behavior, the $Z$ pole resonance and the $s/t$-channel interplay.

item.title: 100 ± Δ t years of quantum uncertainty: From origins to modern insights
item.description: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, marking a decisive departure from classical physics. Conceived almost a century ago through a thought experiment showing that measuring an electron's position inevitably disturbs its momentum, it began as a deceptively simple idea that sparked countless studies and grew into the rich research field it is today.

item.title: Therapeutic communication: avoidance of negative influences and application of beneficial suggestions in anesthesia and intensive care, emergency, and pain medicine
item.description: In anesthesia, and in emergency and intensive care medicine a “therapeutic communication” with the patient is needed that exceeds mere information exchange and that supports patient and treatment. First, ever-present nocebo effects and negative suggestions must be avoided or neutralized.

item.title: Body in memory: the role of bodily self-consciousness in episodic memory and autonoetic consciousness
item.description: Episodic memory (EM) enables the conscious recollection of personally experienced events, including contextual features such as visual, auditory and emotional details. However, the role of bodily signals has been largely neglected in EM, although the observer's body provides a rich bodily context during the encoding, storage and recall of events, and has recently been associated with a bodily form of self-consciousness (bodily self-consciousness; BSC).

item.title: Does Total Knowledge Mute Emotion? A Thought Experiment using Large Language Models
item.description: Abstract This paper examines whether comprehensive knowledge acquisition attenuates emotional experience through a thought experiment that uses large language models (LLMs). We propose that LLMs, which possess extensive propositional knowledge yet lack phenomenal consciousness, serve as philosophical instruments for isolating the knowledge variable from other cognitive attributes.

item.title: Effects of auditory sensory stimulation on consciousness and physiological parameters among individuals with disorders of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: Objective: To systematically evaluate the effects of auditory sensory stimulation (SS) on consciousness levels and physiological parameters in patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC). Furthermore, this study aimed to explore intervention characteristics based on the frequency, intensity, time, and type (FITT) framework that may influence treatment effects and to investigate potential sources of between-study heterogeneity.

item.title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature
item.description: Fragmentation is common in interdisciplinary fields with diverse methods and theoretical commitments. Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve.

item.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
item.description: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons.

item.title: Generalized ladder operators and construction of families of superintegrable systems with Painlevé VI
item.description: We study quantum Hamiltonians whose separated angular component is expressed through a generic Painlevé VI transcendent. We construct generalized ladder operators for one-dimensional Schrödinger operators with a quadratic spectral variable.

item.title: Ergodicity breaking for data classification in a dissipative Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions
item.description: We explore the close relationship between the processing of data and the dynamics of interacting many-body systems. For example, certain classes of quantum neural networks can be mapped onto dissipative quantum Ising models whose evolution is described by a Lindblad master equation.

item.title: Learning to control and predict light-driven electron-phonon dynamics
item.description: Driving lattice vibrations provides a direct route to manipulating electronic correlations through nonlinear electron-phonon coupling. Finding suitable driving fields, however, requires control over the coupled dynamics beyond a simple choice of pulse amplitude and frequency.

item.title: Training quantum neural networks one job at a time
item.description: When a quantum processor is reached through a cloud queue, a variational algorithm pays for every round trip, and a single round trip can carry many circuits. The classical optimizer therefore decides how much is learned per job, not only per shot.

item.title: Measurement-informed dynamical decoupling for fidelity preservation on large-scale quantum processors
item.description: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a key technique for suppressing decoherence and preserving the performance of quantum algorithms. We introduce a measurement-based DD (MDD) protocol that determines control unitary gates from partial measurements of noisy subsystems, with measurement overhead scaling linearly with the number of subsystems.
